newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BAA ponders cargo rail investmen.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BAA ponders cargo rail investmen.

text.p: BAA Plc would be prepared to offer its expertise and possible investment in rail projects to improve London Heathrow Airport cargo operations, said its rail strategy manager Paul Le Blond.

"We would be interested in partnerships and in principle, be prepared to invest in projects that ensure that Heathrow continues to work well as a cargo airport," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"But it is early days yet. We have set up a cargo rail study group to enable us first to understand the market and what it would require in terms of investment," he said.

Le Blond added that prior to BAA deciding to invest 400 million stg in the Heathrow-London Paddington express rail link, due to open in 1998, it first had to identify the market and the competition -- "the number of people making the journey and by what means", he said.

"But air cargo is not as easy to understand as the air passenger market. Railfreight has traditionally been associated with bulky, heavy cargo while airfreight is more concerned with smaller, low-bulk shipments," he said.
"The question is: is there the opportunity for a relationship between the two? That is what we will attempt to define," he said.

Le Blond added that the new study group was closely monitoring a plan drawn up by the FOCAL (Freight Operators' Commercial Access Link) to develop a 100 million stg, 250-acre railfreight terminal near Heathrow.
"We have spoken with this project's instigators. Although we have no direct involvement, their proposals are not incompatible to our way of thinking," he said.
"But this will not be the only such project. Good luck to them all. We will see which one succeeds and if there is a market there to support it," he said.
Le Blond stressed, however, that although BAA would be willing to offer expertise and investment, it did not plan itself to be a rail freight operator.
"Companies such as English, Welsh and Scottish Railway would be in a far better place to do that than us," he said.
In the past, he noted that BAA had owned companies such as freight transport operator Scottish Express International and air cargo handler SkyCare Cargo.

"Sometimes these (direct involvements) have worked, sometimes not. What we want to ensure here is that Heathrow, which has a number of rail lines pretty close by that could be linked up to the airport, works well as a cargo centre," he said.
